pathway_order: SYMPTOM_ONSET_REPORTED <= FIRST_CONTACT <= PHYSICIAN_ASSESSMENT <= REFERRAL_SENT <= REFERRAL_RECEIVED <= DIAGNOSIS <= MDT_DECISION <= SPECIALIST_VISIT <= TREATMENT_START

settings.n_definition: Latent complete episodes before independent event-level missingness; observed n reported per cell.
settings.missingness: Independent per timestamp; endpoint completeness is (1-m)^2, not (1-m).
settings.precision: MONTH dates are stored at the Gregorian month midpoint and flagged; pairs with a MONTH endpoint are excluded from the test. Negative measured spans excluded, zero-day spans logged as 0.5 day, effective n reported.
settings.observation: MONTH dates are interval-valued; they are kept in the data but carry no weight in the mean-log test.
settings.reference: Design grid and early warning: independent fixed synthetic rest-of-country pool per observation condition, conditional Monte Carlo; finite reference SE retained. Null experiments and the rest-of-country check: each county against the other episodes of the same simulated country. The two text-extraction experiments use their own pools of 100000 episodes. The single-county null experiments use the calibration sample as reference.
settings.test: Welch test of mean log-duration with Student t critical values (Welch-Satterthwaite degrees of freedom); a county is tested in an interval only with at least 30 complete day-precision episodes.
settings.month_precision: A date known to the month only is not used in the test: an interval is testable when both of its dates are present and known to the day.
settings.family: One look: 23 counties x 3 intervals = 69 comparisons (a = 0.05/69). The early-warning study counts its 12 planned quarterly looks in the family (a = 0.05/(69 x 12)), a Bonferroni upper bound for overlapping rolling windows. Cancer-site strata are not in the family; each stratum analysed separately multiplies it again.
settings.national_cases: 37000 new cases a year is an assumption used for county sizes; it is not an observed incidence.
settings.monte_carlo_se: Binomial error of the replications plus the sampling error of the one fixed reference mean (delta method on the analytic power); gap_in_monte_carlo_se is only given where the analytic power is between 0.02 and 0.98.
settings.intermediate_events: One pathway order. REFERRAL_RECEIVED = REFERRAL_SENT + min(U(0,3) days, time to DIAGNOSIS); DIAGNOSIS = REFERRAL_SENT + 0.6 x (referral-to-specialist step), an unsourced modelling constant that sets the diagnostic and treatment columns; MDT_DECISION uniform between DIAGNOSIS and SPECIALIST_VISIT, also a modelling choice; TREATMENT_START = SPECIALIST_VISIT + last step. Latent times are cumulative sums of non-negative gaps.
settings.slowdown: A planted slowdown multiplies every gap inside one core interval and shifts all later events.
settings.stage_dependence: Diagnostic span is 0.6 x the referral-to-specialist step; treatment span is 0.4 x that step plus the last step, so the two are positively correlated but not identical.
settings.log_duration: log(days) on whole-day intervals; a zero-day interval is logged as 0.5 day; positive intervals are unchanged.
settings.analytic_power: Normal approximation for the planted interval own two-sided test at Bonferroni 0.05/69, with the measured per-interval log-SD, testable n = n(1-m)^2(1-q)^2 (m: share of dates missing, q: share of dates known to the month only) and the finite reference. The detector uses t quantiles and a minimum n, which the formula does not.
settings.empirical_power: planted_test_power: share of replications where the planted interval own test rejects. county_power (any of the three tests rejects) is kept as a separate outcome.
settings.assumptions: National case count, routes, route shares, distributions, thresholds, censor cutoff and simulated effects are assumptions, not Finnish observations.

sigma_sources.step_sigma: input of the simulator (simulate.SIGMA), a modelling choice; computed from neither the cohort nor the simulator
sigma_sources.per_interval: computed from the simulator: SD of log-duration of each interval in the calibration sample
sigma_sources.cohort_implied: computed from the cohort: sqrt(2 ln(mean/median)) of the published symptom-to-treatment mean and median, per route

cohort_check.reading: The simulator reproduces the published mean but not the published median: five independent steps sum to a total that is much less skewed than the cohort. Real intervals may be more spread than the simulated ones, which would raise every required n.

interval_log_sd.definition: Whole-day dates, no missing events, DAY precision. log-duration = log(days), a zero-day interval is logged as 0.5 day; positive intervals are unchanged.

sample_sizes.rest_of_country_formula: n (N - n) / N >= s^2 (z_{1-a/2} + z_power)^2 / (ln r)^2, N = episodes in the country in the period

sample_size_check_summary.monte_carlo_se: sqrt(binomial variance of the replications + variance from the sampling error of the one fixed reference mean)

measured_text_extraction.error_model: Each date: signed error drawn independently from the measured list of its profile; each event: lost with the measured missing share. Negative spans are excluded, never repaired.

The confirmed condition assumes that a person removes every error; that was not measured.

measured_interval_extraction.error_model: Each core interval of a simulated episode gets an error drawn from the measured within-note interval errors of the profile (predicted span minus true span over pairs of DAY-precision gold events of one note whose two endpoints were found) and is lost with the measured lost share. Negative spans are excluded, never repaired.
measured_interval_extraction.extra_events_model: Measured per writer and event type; an episode slot receives an extra with probability 1 - exp(-9 x extras of the type / gold events). An extra makes both core intervals that use the slot underivable, because eventlog.intervals.derive needs exactly one start and one end event. An extra that stands in for a true event missing from the record is not modelled.
limits: The error profiles come from 700 SYNTHETIC test notes written and labelled by language models, not from clinical text; the test notes had been read before (post hoc).
The resolver was designed on the generator's own six date forms; notes with other relative phrasings are not represented.
Interval errors are drawn from all within-note pairs, not per interval type; extra events that stand in for a missing true event are not modelled.
The confirmed condition assumes that a person removes every error; that was not measured.

findings: One pathway order is used by simulator, validator and document: SYMPTOM_ONSET_REPORTED <= FIRST_CONTACT <= PHYSICIAN_ASSESSMENT <= REFERRAL_SENT <= REFERRAL_RECEIVED <= DIAGNOSIS <= MDT_DECISION <= SPECIALIST_VISIT <= TREATMENT_START. In 50000000 simulated episodes rounded to whole days it is violated 0 times.
The synthetic Parquet sample of 20000 episodes and 177958 events validates with 0 chronology violations, 0 duplicates and 0 impossible dates.
The design grid contains 960 design cells with 1000 replications per cell.

Measured standard deviation of log-duration in 50000000 simulated episodes (whole days, zero-day intervals logged as 0.5 day): primary care 0.9383, diagnostic 0.9773, treatment 0.8035; the idealised single-step value is 0.96. Wider than idealised: diagnostic; narrower: primary care, treatment.
By route (fast, public) the standard deviation of log-duration is: primary care 0.9112, 0.7465; diagnostic 0.9642, 0.9627; treatment 0.7677, 0.8267.
Share of zero-day intervals in that sample: primary care 0.000007, diagnostic 0.000292, treatment 0.000010.

Cohort check, public route, symptom onset to treatment start (2000000 simulated episodes): simulated mean 207.1 days, median 174.0, log-SD 0.548; published mean 207, median 127, implied log-SD 0.988. The simulator matches the published mean, not the published median.
Idealised sizing (s = 0.96) requires 1809, 495, 239 and 100 complete episodes for 10%, 20%, 30% and 50% slowdowns; with the cohort-implied spread (s = 0.9885) it requires 1917, 524, 253 and 106.
Per-interval sizing for primary care (s = 0.9383) requires 1728, 473, 228 and 96 complete episodes for 10%, 20%, 30% and 50% slowdowns.
Per-interval sizing for diagnostic (s = 0.9773) requires 1874, 513, 248 and 104 complete episodes for 10%, 20%, 30% and 50% slowdowns.
Per-interval sizing for treatment (s = 0.8035) requires 1267, 347, 168 and 70 complete episodes for 10%, 20%, 30% and 50% slowdowns.

With the rest of the country as comparator (37000 episodes a year, an assumption) a 10% slowdown requires primary care 1817, diagnostic 1980, treatment 1314; against one quarter (9250 episodes) a 20% slowdown requires primary care 499, diagnostic 545, treatment 361.

Formula check at exactly the per-interval n (200000 replications in each of 12 cells), with the measured SD treated as known as the formula assumes: simulated power ranges from 0.8001 to 0.8058; the largest gap to the analytic power is 0.0032 (diagnostic, 50% slowdown, n = 104), 3.26 Monte Carlo standard errors; 1 of 12 cells are beyond 3 standard errors.

Same cells with the detector as run (variance estimated in each county, t quantiles): simulated power ranges from 0.7570 to 0.8008; the largest gap to the analytic power is 0.0431 (treatment, 50% slowdown, n = 70), 45.20 Monte Carlo standard errors; 8 of 12 cells are beyond 3 standard errors.

Mean signed gap of the detector (simulated minus analytic power) by interval: primary care -0.0181 (skewness of log-duration -0.169), diagnostic -0.0108 (skewness of log-duration -0.022), treatment -0.0144 (skewness of log-duration +0.164).

Rest-of-country comparator, fully simulated (2000 replications per cell): at the infinite-reference n the power is 0.759 to 0.783 for a 20% slowdown against one quarter and 0.761 to 0.783 for a 10% slowdown against one year; at the two-sample n it is 0.789 to 0.803 and 0.792 to 0.814.

In the design grid at day precision without missing events the largest gap between the planted interval's simulated power and its per-interval analytic power is 0.0557 (primary care, n = 100, 50% slowdown; 1 of the 30 cells with analytic power between 0.02 and 0.98 are beyond 3 Monte Carlo standard errors).

Largest gap by observation condition (missingness, month-precision share), with month-precision pairs left out of the test and counted out of n in the formula: (0.0, 0.0) 0.0557; (0.0, 0.5) 0.1577; (0.2, 0.0) 0.0846; (0.2, 0.5) 0.0882.
The largest gap over all observation conditions is 0.1577 (missingness 0.0, month-precision share 0.5, treatment, n = 100, 50% slowdown: simulated 0.0380 against analytic 0.1957).

Month precision costs episodes instead of validity: with half of the dates known to the month only, a quarter of the intervals are testable. 24 of the 240 D3 cells expect fewer than 30 testable episodes and are not tested at all.
Under the first implementation's definition (any of the three tests rejects, s = 0.96) the largest gap is 0.2421.
The binomial target comparison requires 385 episodes.
D3 county power at n=500 and a 20% slowdown without observation loss ranges from 0.7900 to 0.9530 across planted stages.
